evidence: Upward movement at 382.812 seconds, followed by an unsupported descent. The foreground leg obscures the release mechanism. Height is the student's retrospective estimate, not a calibrated video measurement.

assumptions.status: Working assumptions from a personal-size bottle, quarter fill and half a small box. Product capacity, box size and dry mass are unverified. The green ground support is excluded.

shots.speech: This is my final test with the finished rocket.
There it goes. I estimated about one metre, still below my five metre goal.
My first version reached about two metres, the larger bottle half a metre, and the finished design one metre. That is forty, ten and twenty percent of the goal. The first version went highest.

For an estimate, I used a four hundred millilitre bottle as the starting point. A quarter full gives about one hundred millilitres of vinegar. Half of a fifty gram box gives twenty five grams of baking soda.
The fins help direction, but the fins and tape also add weight. A larger bottle needs more gas for the same pressure increase. Leaks, tilt and friction with the support could also reduce the flight.
The mixture starts near one hundred twenty five grams. Adding an assumed sixty gram dry rocket gives about one hundred eighty five grams before release.

I did not reach five metres. I would start with the lighter version, weigh each part, check the seal, and repeat the test while changing one thing at a time. A more finished appearance did not mean a higher flight.
